result.text: Title: Car Service The police has a new app to remind you of your car service.
The process is started after a successful service.
When a service is necessary, the system checks if your car is still registered.
If it is registered, you are notified.
If you do not go to the service, you are fined after 30 days.
At the car service facility the mechanic enters the problems of your car for reference.
While you wait (can take several days), you get status updates via email.
You can pay through the app, when the repair is done.
The mechanic enters that the repair was successful and you got your "Pickerl".
The mechanic enters the time for you next service.

result.rule: Use an event-based gateway when the first occurring event selects the path. Target supported catching events or receive tasks, not ordinary tasks.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.

Respect event positions: a none intermediate event is catch-only in normal flow and never on a boundary; link events are intermediate-only, thrown and caught in pairs at the same process level, and a catching link has no incoming sequence flow; terminate is an end event only.
Give the outgoing sequence flows of an event-based gateway no conditionExpression; the first occurring target event selects the path.

Give every process and every expanded subProcess its own explicit start event and end event. A trigger that occurs after the main flow (for example later feedback or a return) is joined to the main flow by a gateway, or modeled as an event subprocess or a separate process.

result.rule: When the description does not justify a specialized construct, use the simplest compatible BPMN construct and do not guess missing semantics.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.

result.rule: When the description states an activity or decision with a particular action, condition, scope, or criterion: Label the corresponding BPMN activity or gateway concisely and faithfully, preserving distinctions relevant to the described action or decision rather than substituting unrelated meaning.

When the description distinguishes related actions, events, or outcomes that could otherwise be confused: Label each BPMN element so the stated distinctions remain clear; do not substitute a related action or use a generic label that could refer to multiple described actions or outcomes.

When the description states an activity and provides criteria or other supporting details that are not needed to identify that activity: Label the BPMN element with a concise name for the stated action; omit supporting details that do not distinguish it from another modeled activity, while preserving details that are themselves distinct actions or alternatives.

When the description states a meaningful object, recipient, or responsible role for an activity: Use a concise BPMN label that preserves the described action and those details when they distinguish or clarify the activity.
